title: Customer acquisition strategy: What it is, why it matters, and how to master it
summary: A customer acquisition strategy is how brands attract and convert new customers. See the channels, proven examples, and metrics that drive real growth.
body_markdown:
A customer acquisition strategy is a structured, repeatable approach to attracting and converting new customers across channels, aligning marketing, sales, and service from first awareness through to purchase.


Customer acquisition matters because new customers generate the revenue that funds growth and offsets the attrition every business faces over time—and a strong strategy does that in a way that stays cost-effective and sets those customers up for retention.


This guide covers what a customer acquisition strategy is, the channels that power it, proven strategies backed by real brand examples, and the metrics that tell you whether it's working.


### **TL;DR**


- A customer acquisition strategy is a repeatable system for attracting and converting new customers across channels, guiding them from awareness to purchase and into retention.
- The acquisition funnel runs through three core stages—awareness, consideration, and conversion—with each stage doing a distinct job in moving prospects toward becoming customers.
- Acquisition and retention are two halves of the same growth engine: acquisition adds new revenue, retention maximizes lifetime value, and neither works well in isolation.
- The strongest programs orchestrate channels around first-party data, pairing search, social, cross-channel engagement, and integrated advertising rather than relying on any single one.
- Success is measured against customer acquisition cost (CAC) and customer lifetime value (CLV), with AI sharpening targeting through predictive lead scoring and individual-level decisioning.


## What is a customer acquisition strategy?


A customer acquisition strategy is a structured, repeatable approach to attracting and converting new customers across channels. It aligns marketing, sales, and service around a single job: guiding prospects from first awareness through to purchase.


A strong strategy uses data to focus effort and spend on the audiences most likely to convert and stay. Those prospects move through the customer acquisition funnel's three core stages:


**Awareness:** where they first discover the brand


**Consideration:** where they weigh it against alternatives


**Conversion:** where they decide to buy.


Acquisition connects directly to retention, because when a strong strategy guides new customers into a deliberate retention experience, it turns first purchases into repeat custom and loyalty. This lowers acquisition costs over time by getting more value from every customer won.


## Customer acquisition vs. retention (and vs. marketing)


Acquisition, retention, and marketing all drive growth, but in different ways. This is how they differ and how they work together:


**Acquisition is** the work of winning new customers and generating first-time revenue, measured by whether a prospect becomes a buyer.


**Retention is** the work of keeping existing customers engaged and maximizing their lifetime value. The most effective businesses balance the two, since acquisition without retention loses customers as fast as it gains them.


**Marketing is** the broader discipline both sit inside, covering positioning, brand building, audience strategy, and demand generation across the full customer relationship.


## Customer acquisition channels


Customer acquisition channels are the paths you use to reach potential customers, get them familiar with your brand, and move them toward buying. From paid and organic search to traditional advertising, some build awareness, some nurture interest, some drive the sale.


Here's how the main channels compare at a glance:


Channel


What it does


Where it fits


Organic & paid search


SEO earns steady, low-cost visibility over time; PPC pays for instant placement at the top


Catching people the moment they search


Organic & paid social


Organic builds trust and identity; paid ads extend reach fast with targeting


Meeting people where they already spend time


Cross-channel engagement (email, push, in-app, SMS)

Moving interested people to buy, then to buy again

Broad reach you can actually track when tied back to digital


Adding scale without losing measurement


### Organic and paid search


Search catches people right when they're looking. Organic search is the long game—good SEO earns you steady, low-cost visibility over time. Paid search (PPC) is the shortcut: you pay to show up at the top the moment someone searches. Run both and you're there whether they're still researching or ready to buy.


### Organic and paid social


Social meets people where they already spend their time. Organic social builds trust and a sense of who you are through content and conversation. Paid social speeds that up with targeted ads. Test as you go, so your budget chases actual conversions and not likes and follows.


### Cross-channel engagement marketing


Your owned channels—email, push, in-app messages, and SMS—let you build a direct relationship from the very first interaction, on channels you actually control. A well-timed welcome series, an early offer, or something genuinely useful can nudge someone from curious to customer. Strong[customer engagement](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-engagement-guide) here is often what turns a one-time buyer into a repeat one.


### Traditional advertising integrated with digital


TV, radio, and billboards still pull their weight, as long as you tie them back to something digital. Put a QR code on the billboard, retarget the people who saw your TV spot, and suddenly you can track what that broad reach actually did for you.


### First-party data and orchestration as the connective tissue


None of this works in isolation. Channels only pay off when they talk to each other, and that runs on data. With privacy rules tightening and third-party cookies fading,[first-party data](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/a-complete-guide-to-first-party-data) that your customers share with you directly is what keeps your targeting sharp and compliant.[Journey orchestration](https://www.braze.com/product/journey-orchestration) is what connects it all, so what someone does on one channel shapes what they get on the next, and the whole thing feels like one conversation instead of a dozen disconnected messages.


## Proven customer acquisition strategies (with real examples)


The clearest way to see what a customer acquisition strategy can do is to watch one work. The seven strategies below each pair a proven approach with a real brand that ran it, and the metric it moved. Use them as a starting point, then adapt to your own audience and goals.


### 1. Data-driven personalization


**Strategy:** Personalization helps brands acquire high-value customers faster by delivering relevant content and offers from the first interaction.


**How it works:** First-party data is what makes those experiences feel tailored rather than generic, and relevance is what drives conversion.


**Example:** Digital publisher[Tapas](https://www.braze.com/customers/tapas-case-study) used first-party data and action-based triggers to deliver personalized recommendations, driving a 100% increase in user retention.


### 2. Referral and incentive programs


**Strategy:** Referral programs turn happy customers into an acquisition channel by rewarding them for bringing in new users.


**How it works:** Well-designed incentives, like discounts or perks, encourage more people to act while keeping acquisition costs low.


**Example:**[Wealthsimple](https://www.braze.com/customers/wealthsimple-case-study) , a leading Canadian money management platform, offered a complimentary mobile device to clients who transferred a set amount of assets, contributing to a 40% increase in quarterly net deposits.


### 3. Cross-channel engagement


**Strategy:** Reaching prospects across email, push, in-app messaging, and paid media creates a coordinated acquisition experience.


**How it works:** Brands that connect their channels tend to see higher engagement and stronger conversion than those running each in isolation.


**Example:**[Grubhub](https://www.braze.com/customers/grubhub-onboarding-case-study) used Braze to promote its Grubhub Campus offering across email and push, increasing Grubhub+ sign-ups by 188% versus a control group and driving an 836% increase in ROI.


### 4. Search and social optimization


**Strategy:** Optimizing paid search, organic search, and paid social helps brands reach high-intent prospects at the right moment.


**How it works:** First-party data sharpens audience targeting, which brings acquisition costs down.


**Example:**[ClassPass](https://www.braze.com/customers/classpass-case-study) integrated Braze Audience Sync to automate real-time customer segmentation across Google, TikTok, and Facebook, lifting conversion rates by 2% on TikTok.


### 5. Gated content and lead generation


**Strategy:** Offering something valuable—an exclusive report, a webinar, a members' program—attracts prospects and builds a quality lead pipeline.


**How it works:** Nurturing those leads with personalized follow-ups is what turns interest into conversion.


**Example:**[Virgin Red](https://www.braze.com/customers/virgin-red-case-study) , the loyalty program of the Virgin Group, streamlined its email engagement by integrating Braze with Snowflake, driving a 45% open rate on its IP warmup campaign, with 7,000+ members clicking through to its Friend Referral Program and a healthy rise in new member sign-ups.


### 6. Onboarding and activation


**Strategy:** Onboarding is where acquisition either sticks or slips.


**How it works:** If new users don't reach value quickly, they leave before the relationship starts, so guided onboarding and activation flows are a direct lever on conversion and long-term retention.


**Example:**[Hosco](https://www.braze.com/customers/hosco-case-study) built multi-path onboarding flows based on user behavior, leading to 10,000 job applications and stronger long-term engagement.


### 7. AI and predictive targeting


**Strategy:** AI-powered automation helps brands acquire and engage prospects more efficiently.


**How it works:** It uses predictive lead scoring and real-time engagement triggers to sharpen targeting with far less manual effort.


**Example:**[8fit](https://www.braze.com/customers/8fit-case-study-predictive) used[BrazeAI™](https://www.braze.com/product/brazeai) to score users by their likelihood to purchase, driving 3.75X higher conversions than campaigns run without predictive targeting.


## How to measure customer acquisition


You measure customer acquisition by tracking the cost, efficiency, and long-term value of the customers you win. Here are the metrics to look out for:


### Customer acquisition cost (CAC)


Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the total amount spent to gain a new customer, including marketing and sales expenses like advertising, content creation, and sales team costs. A high CAC without a strong return points to inefficiency in your marketing or sales process, so the aim is to keep CAC as low as you can while still bringing in quality customers.


### Customer lifetime value (CLV) and the CLV:CAC ratio


Where CAC tells you what a customer costs to win, customer lifetime value (CLV) tells you how much revenue that customer is likely to generate over the whole relationship. The two work as a pair. Comparing them—the CLV:CAC ratio—is what shows whether acquisition is actually profitable. CLV should sit comfortably above CAC, so the money you spend to acquire someone earns back more than it cost over time.


### Conversion rate, payback period, and channel performance


Beyond those two headline numbers, three more metrics sharpen the picture of how acquisition is performing:


- **Conversion rate:** The share of leads that become paying customers. A low rate usually points to a targeting or messaging problem earlier in the funnel.
- **Payback period:** How long it takes to recoup what you spent to acquire a customer. The shorter it is, the sooner that cash is free to reinvest.
- **Channel performance:** Which channels bring in the most valuable customers at the lowest cost, so you can put budget where it works hardest.


Watched together over time, these numbers show where acquisition is efficient and where money is leaking out. Increasingly, spotting those patterns and acting on them is work AI can do faster than any manual analysis.


## How AI improves customer acquisition


AI improves customer acquisition by analyzing large volumes of data to identify patterns and predict customer behavior, which powers personalized marketing and more efficient targeting. These areas make the biggest difference.


### Predictive lead scoring


Predictive lead scoring uses AI to analyze user behavior and engagement patterns and estimate how likely each prospect is to convert. That lets teams prioritize outreach and put marketing resources behind high-potential prospects instead of spreading spend evenly.[Predictive analytics](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/predictive-customer-analytics) sits behind this, turning raw behavior into a score you can act on.


### Personalized outreach


AI segments audiences by behavior and preference and helps build dynamic content that adapts to each user's profile. The more relevant the message, the more likely a prospect is to engage and, eventually, convert.


### Automated real-time engagement


AI-driven automation lets brands run campaigns that respond to user actions the moment they happen. If someone shows interest in a product but doesn't complete a purchase, an automated follow-up can nudge them toward conversion, and AI-powered chat can answer questions and guide prospects to the next step.


### Smarter targeting and audience sync


AI also sharpens targeting on paid channels.[Audience sync](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/build-more-relevant-and-cost-effective-ads-with-braze-audience-sync) pushes first-party segments to platforms like Google, Meta, and TikTok as behavior changes, so ad targeting stays relevant and budget isn't spent on people who have already converted.


### Generative AI vs. action optimization


It helps to separate two jobs AI does here. Generative AI, like[BrazeAI™](https://www.braze.com/product/brazeai) , creates outreach content and variants—subject lines, copy, creative—quickly and at scale. Action optimization decides what to send: it selects the right message, channel, and moment for each prospect and scores how likely each lead is to convert. At its most advanced, an AI decisioning system can make 1:1 decisions that optimize any business KPI, choosing across message, channel, offer, timing, and frequency for each individual rather than applying one rule to a whole segment.


These capabilities make acquisition sharper and faster, though they deliver most when they sit inside a clear, deliberate strategy.


## How to build and refine your customer acquisition strategy


The strongest customer acquisition strategies aim for the right customers, not the most. This five-step framework builds a repeatable process for winning them and keeps acquisition tied to retention from the start.


Step


What to do


Why it matters


1. Define your ICP


Pin down who your highest-value customers are and what they need


Focuses effort on prospects worth winning


1. Align sales and marketing


Get both teams working to the same targets and message


Keeps the journey consistent for the prospect


1. Choose and orchestrate channels


Pick the channels your audience uses and connect them


Channels reinforce each other instead of competing


1. Invest in onboarding and activation


Guide new customers to value quickly


A conversion that never activates is money lost


1. Measure and optimize


Track CAC and CLV and refine continuously


Keeps acquisition profitable and connected to retention


### 1. Define your ideal customer profile


Start by defining your ideal customer profile (ICP): who needs what you offer, what problem they're solving, and what a high-value customer looks like. A clear ICP focuses your spend on the prospects most worth winning, which is the difference between acquiring the most customers and acquiring the right ones.


### 2. Align sales and marketing


Get sales and marketing working from the same definition of a good customer and the same message. When both teams share targets and targeting, prospects get one coherent journey instead of a disjointed experience as they move from first touch to purchase.


### 3. Choose and orchestrate channels


Pick the channels where your audience already spends time, then orchestrate them so they reinforce each other rather than compete. A signal on one channel should shape what happens on the next, which is what makes a set of separate campaigns feel like a single conversation.


### 4. Invest in onboarding and activation


Treat onboarding and activation with the same seriousness as the top of the funnel. A prospect who converts but never reaches value is a customer you've paid for and lost, so guiding new customers to their first win protects the return on everything you spent to acquire them. A focused approach to[improving acquisition](https://www.braze.com/solutions/improve-acquisition) pays off here.


### 5. Measure and optimize against CAC and CLV


Measure everything against CAC and CLV, and use what you learn to refine targeting, channels, and messaging over time. Keep the connection to[retention](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/complete-guide-to-retention-marketing) part of the plan, not an afterthought—acquiring the right customers and setting them up to stay is what turns acquisition into a long-term investment rather than a recurring cost.
